objectives: Students will study the U.S. governance system and the role of law in education.
Students will study the relationship between the individual and the state.
Students will study applicable federal and state constitutional provisions, statutes, regulations, and case law.
Students will explore the application of these laws in schools.
Students will study applicable standards of professional ethics for educators.
Students will explore the application of these standards through case scenarios and current events.
Students will learn basic methods of law-related research.

Students will demonstrate and be able to appropriately apply, in context, the most significant federal and state constitutional provisions, statutes, regulations, and case law decisions governing education.
topics: 1) Governance theory, structures, and the legal system.
2) The legal relationship between the individual and the state.
3) Church-State law.
4) Free speech law.
5) Due process law and student discipline.
6) Grading policies, FERPA, and open records laws.
7) Juvenile laws, custody, compulsory attendance, and delinquency.
8) Mandatory reporting statutes for child abuse and neglect.
9) Search and seizure law.
10) Equal protection of the laws and equity issues.
11) Special education law.
12) Contract law.
13) Tort law.
14) Teacher tenure and fair dismissal law.

Students will be able to produce a precis of the dissertation proposal, containing relevant literature and research methods.
